title: Session-based authentication
idea: Session-based authentication keeps the login on the server: it stores a session after a correct password, and the browser holds only a random session id.

analogy.text: A coat check. You hand over your coat and get a numbered ticket; the cloakroom keeps the coat, and you carry only the ticket.
analogy.breaks: A ticket is shown once; a session id travels with every request.

points: A cookie is a value the browser stores and sends back automatically.
`httpOnly` hides the cookie from page JavaScript, so a script cannot read the id.
On each request, the server looks the id up to learn who is calling.
Logout deletes the session, so a copied id stops working at once.

hero.title: A session from login to logout

messages.label: POST /login
messages.note: The browser sends email and password, once.

messages.label: check password
messages.note: The server compares the password with the stored hash.

messages.label: set(sid, user 1)
messages.note: It creates a random id and stores the session under it.

messages.label: Set-Cookie: sid
messages.note: The id goes back in a cookie. The browser keeps it.

messages.label: GET /me + Cookie
messages.note: Every later request carries the cookie automatically.

messages.label: get(sid)
messages.note: The server looks the id up.

messages.label: user 1
messages.note: The session names the user, so the request is Ada's.

messages.label: POST /logout
messages.note: On logout the browser sends the cookie once more.

messages.label: delete(sid)
messages.note: The server deletes the session. The id is dead, even if someone copied it.

code.title: Login, /me and logout
code.caption: `demo-password` is a demo value. The `Map` is lost on restart; the next page moves sessions to Postgres.

walk.text: Stand-ins: one user with a hashed password, and a `Map` that will hold sessions.
`cookieParser()` fills `req.cookies` from the `Cookie` header, as `express.json()` fills `req.body`.
Find the user and check the password. Either failure gives the same `401` message.
Store the session under a random id. Send only the id, in a cookie that limits cross-site sending.
Later requests: look the cookie's id up. No session means `401`; otherwise you know the user.
Logout deletes the session on the server, then clears the browser's cookie.
The script calls its own server and copies the cookie by hand, as a browser would.

pitfalls: Make ids with `crypto.randomUUID()`. Counters or user ids are easy to guess.
Delete the session on logout; clearing only the cookie leaves a copied id valid.
Set `secure: true` when serving HTTPS, so browsers never send the cookie over HTTP.

quiz.why: Deleting the entry removes the server's record, so the old id gives `nobody`. An id that never existed does too.

takeaway: Treat the session id like a password: random, protected, and deleted on logout.

starters: Why store an id in the cookie instead of the user's email?
What happens if someone steals a session id?
Should I use `express-session` instead of writing this by hand?
